title: Example 110: an Idempotency-Key header on POST /orders drops the body's @Valid, caught by the boundary contract (B12)
description: The first example of approach B12, boundary contracts: jvmcontract reads the Spring annotations of the ticketing-service classes and checks them against src/contract/boundaries.contract. The patch adds an Idempotency-Key header parameter to OrderController#place and loses the @Valid on the request body. Expected: a violation with two boundary changes (the old POST /orders line removed, the new one added without @Valid). The runner compiles the patched module with Gradle (offline, from the Gradle cache) and runs jvmcontract verify; the module's Spring Boot tests run first and need Docker for Testcontainers, so they may fail without it, which the page records separately from the verdict.
expected: build.py 110 exits 0: verdict violation, 2 boundary changes, matches expected
